finalText:
Found it: `processOrder.js` acquired a connection directly and only called `pool.release` on the line after `run()` — so any rejected order (bad payload) skipped the release entirely. The logs match exactly: each `invalid order payload` error bumped "pool in-use" by one and never gave it back, until the pool hit 5/5 and both the worker and the API started throwing `pool exhausted` / `acquire timeout`, ending in the 2am restarts.

Fixed by wrapping the acquire in try/finally, same pattern `api.js` already used via `withConnection`. All 4 tests pass now, 71ms.
